（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
C. I. D. REGISTRY
No. Central Station.
687
Date 27-11-29
Date November 25th 1929.
File No.）
Subject (in full) Attached Newspaper Cutting.
Made by D. I. Hunter. Forwarded by
With reference to attached, I interviewed Mr. King, Sub-
Manager of the Bank of China on the 23rd November 1929, who stated
that other than the eight ( 8 ) persons arrested in the French
Concession by the French and Chinese Authorities, and the seizure
of the complete printing plant, no further arrests were made. Mr.
King further stated that the complete gang of counterfeiters had
been captured and from information obtained from the prisoners
under arrest there were no others connected with the counterfeit-
ing in the International Settlement.
The French Police were also interviewed and stated that no
further arrests were expected in connection with the case.
Attached are specimens of the uncompleted notes received
from the French Police.

1, 1929. TIMES, THURSDAY, NOVEMBER 21, 1929.

COUNTERFEITERS ARE
TAKEN AT WORK

7 Chinese Caught Making
Spurious $5 Bank Of
China Notes

A lightning raid by French police on a counterfeiting establishment in the French Concession yesterday afternoon, resulted in the arrest of seven Chinese and the seizure of 6,000 partially-completed Bank of China notes of $5 denomination, a large quantity of banknote paper, several printing presses and other paraphernalia.

The raid was carried out so suddenly and thoroughly that the seven Chinese arrested were caught red-handed in the act of printing the spurious money. The seven will be brought up to-morrow morning in the French Provisional Court for trial.

The arrest of the counterfeiters was carried out by the French police co-operating with detectives from the office of the Woosung and Shanghai Garrison Commander. The appearance in the Chinese city during the last two weeks of a number of spurious $5 Bank of China notes, led to an investigation being made by the Chinese detectives and the trail led to a Chinese house in a leyway off Rue Amiral Bayle.

Early yesterday morning, the Chinese detectives informed the French police of the result of their investigation, and plans were then made to raid the house in which the counterfeiters were believed to be manufacturing the spurious money.

Shortly before 3 p.m. a detail of French foreign and Chinese detectives and detectives from the office of the Woosung and Shanghai Garrison Commander, swooped down suddenly on the suspected house. The dwelling was surrounded by the police and without any preliminaries, the front door forced.

As the police made their way into the house, a Chinese rushed out of one of the rooms, but before he could give an alarm, he was seized. The police made their way into one of the rooms on the ground floor and found six other Chinese there, making test prints on the reverse sides of several of the partially completed banknotes.

No resistance was made by the Chinese and a thorough search of the house was made by the police. In an upstairs room was found bundles of the half-completed $5 Bank of China notes, and a large quantity of banknote paper, while downstairs were the printing presses and other equipment. Five plates were also seized. According to the French police, the spurious notes were so excellent that it would take an expert to distinguish the difference between them and real Bank of China notes of the same denomination.

1, 1929. 《泰晤士报》，1929年11月21日，星期四。

伪造者
作案时被捕

7名中国人因制造
假中国银行5元券
被抓获

昨天下午，法国警察对法租界内一处伪造窝点进行了闪电式突袭，结果逮捕了7名中国人，并缴获了6000张未完工的中国银行5元面额钞票、大量钞票用纸、数台印刷机及其他辅助工具。

此次突袭行动迅速且彻底，被捕的7名中国人在印制假币时被当场抓获。这7人将于明天上午在法国临时法庭受审。

此次对伪造者的逮捕是由法国警察与吴淞上海警备司令部办公室的侦探合作执行的。过去两周内，华界出现了一些假的中国银行5元券，导致中国侦探展开调查，线索指向贝勒海军上将路（Rue Amiral Bayle）旁一条小巷内的一所中国住宅。

昨天清晨，中国侦探向法国警察通报了调查结果，随后制定了突袭该住宅的计划，据信伪造者正在其中制造假币。

下午3点前不久，一队法国外籍和中国侦探以及来自吴淞上海警备司令部办公室的侦探突然袭击了这所可疑住宅。警察包围了该住所，没有任何预警便强行打开了前门。

当警察进入屋内时，一名中国人从一个房间冲出来，但在他发出警报之前就被抓住了。警察进入一楼的一个房间，发现另外6名中国人在那里，正在几张未完工的钞票背面进行测试印刷。

中国人未作抵抗，警察对房屋进行了彻底搜查。在楼上的房间里发现了成捆的半成品中国银行5元券和大量钞票用纸，而楼下则是印刷机和其他设备。还缴获了5块印版。据法国警察称，这些假钞制作精良，需要专家才能区分它们与同面额的真中国银行钞票之间的差异。
